description: Found by defk-t11.4: defk-juw's lost-resume check (F->resume cleared on arrival at the safepoint's loop) misses (1) a wrong dispatch case that jumps to another loop's label: it still clears F->resume, so the kernel silently gives a wrong answer; (2) nested loops where the top-level case is missing: the inner loop's dispatch still finds and clears the resume after the outer loop restarted. Consider clearing only when the arrived-at safepoint id equals F->resume (compare ids, not just clear), keeping zero loop cost. Done when the t11.4 mutation harness (test/resume_test.exs lost_mutant/2) has a wrong-label and a nested-missing case that both raise.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The lost-resume check clears the saved resume point only when the safepoint it arrives at is the one saved, so a dispatch to the wrong loop or a missing outer dispatch raises instead of giving a wrong answer

**Current behavior:**
On resume, the frame's resume point (F->resume) is cleared on arrival at a safepoint's loop (defk-juw), and a resume never cleared raises. This misses (1) a wrong dispatch case that jumps to another loop's label: it still clears F->resume, so the kernel silently gives a wrong answer; (2) nested loops where the top-level case is missing: the inner loop's dispatch finds and clears the resume after the outer loop restarted.

**Desired behavior:**
Arrival clears the resume only when the arrived-at safepoint id equals the saved one; any other arrival with a pending resume is the existing internal resume error. Zero added cost inside loops on the non-resume path (the comparison happens only when a resume is pending).

**Key interfaces:**
- Resume dispatch and the lost-resume check in the generated C / runtime header; the mutation harness in the resume tests (lost_mutant/2)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Mutation harness gains a wrong-label case and a nested-missing-top-level case; both raise the resume error
- [ ] Existing resume, forced-yield and upgrade tests pass
- [ ] No change in the generated hot loop on the non-resume path (check the C or a microbench), noted in the report
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Redesigning resume dispatch (see defk-w8l notes on defk_rs)

title: Resume check can't catch a dispatch to the wrong loop
